docs.title: About me
docs.text:
I hold a PhD in Applied Mathematics from the University of Strasbourg, where I conducted my research at the Institut de Recherche Mathématique Avancée (IRMA), a Joint Research Unit (UMR 7501) of the CNRS. My PhD thesis, entitled Model Order Reduction Methods for Hamiltonian Dynamics Using Deep Learning, focused on the use of deep learning techniques for model order reduction of Hamiltonian dynamical systems.

I am currently a postdoctoral researcher at the CERFACS in Toulouse, working within the CONCACE team on hybrid AI-enhanced large-scale iterative methods.

docs.title: Domain & activity
docs.text:
Since September 2026, I have been a postdoctoral researcher within the CONCACE team, based at CERFACS in Toulouse. My research focuses on hybrid AI-enhanced large-scale iterative methods.

From October 2021 to September 2025, I was a PhD student within the MOCO and MACARON teams. My research focused on model order reduction (MOR) for Hamiltonian systems.

docs.title: CEMRACS summer school 2022
docs.text: I participated in CEMRACS 2022 on the theme "Transport in Physics, Biology, and Urban Traffic". I took part in a project titled "Model order reduction in velocity space and learning for the Vlasov-Maxwell equations" which resulted in a publication doi:10.1051/proc/202477213.
